text:
San Jose is 11-14-2 with a 4% shot at the playoffs by our numbers, which is about what a rebuilding team with this many teenagers should look like. The Sharks give up a lot: 3.71 expected goals against per 60 minutes (expected goals measure the quality of chances), and only 43.7% of the chances overall. They have also scored more than 11 fewer goals than their chances predict, so the record isn't flattering them.

Macklin Celebrini is still the whole point. He leads the club's headlines every week, lost his voice in one game according to San Jose Hockey Now, and keeps stacking power-play points. His line with Will Smith and Ivar Stenberg, or Igor Chernyshov in Stenberg's place, has taken about 60% of the chances. Smith had what San Jose Hockey Now called the best game of his career, a three-point night against Nashville, and Stenberg is earning trust as a rookie.

The defense is where it breaks down. Darnell Nurse and Michael Kesselring have been outscored 15-6 at five on five, Jacob Trouba and Sam Dickinson 10-6. Kiefer Sherwood is on injured reserve, week to week. One more thing to circle: Tyler Toffoli plays his 1,000th NHL game next Thursday at Madison Square Garden, per Max Miller. For this team the season is measured in how fast the kids grow, and the top line is growing quickly.
headline: Celebrini's Sharks are learning in a hard school
